Winery

Domaine Vacheron

Family domaine in Sancerre, in the Loire, known for its biodynamically farmed Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Noir and for its single-parcel wines.

Domaine Vacheron is a family estate based in the town of Sancerre itself, at the top of the hill overlooking the appellation’s vineyards. Several generations of the Vacheron family have worked these vines, and in recent decades the cousins Jean-Laurent and Jean-Dominique Vacheron, followed by the next generation, have given the domaine a considerable international profile.

One of the hallmarks of the house is its commitment to biodynamic farming, adopted across the whole vineyard in the early 21st century, together with hand harvesting and fermentation with indigenous yeasts. The domaine has also worked on identifying Sancerre’s different soils — flint, Kimmeridgian limestones known locally as terres blanches, and limestone pebbles called caillottes — in order to make single-parcel wines.

Vacheron is known for both its Sauvignon Blanc whites and its Pinot Noir reds, a variety that plays a secondary role in Sancerre but to which the house has paid particular attention. Alongside its entry-level Sancerre white, red and rosé, it makes single-parcel wines such as Les Romains, a white, and Belle Dame, a red, both from flint soils.

The domaine’s style aims for precise, fresh wines, focused more on the mineral expression of the soil than on aromatic exuberance, with discreet use of oak for the single-parcel wines.
